note.text:
Intellectual property (IP) is a creation of the mind: inventions, books, music, films, software, designs, brand names.
Protection:
• Copyright protects creative works (books, music, software code) automatically; copying or sharing without permission is illegal.
• Patents protect inventions for a number of years.
• Trademarks protect brand names and logos.
Breaking IP rights: software piracy (illegal copies), plagiarism (presenting others' work as yours), counterfeiting.
In Cameroon, copyright is protected by law and organisations such as SOCAM (music); OAPI handles patents and trademarks for member states.
Respect IP: buy or use licensed software, cite your sources, ask permission.

sections.heading: Ideas can be owned
sections.text:
Intellectual property (IP) means creations of the mind: inventions, books, songs, films, photographs, software and brand names. Creators have rights over how their work is used.
Protecting IP rewards people for their creativity and encourages them to keep creating.

sections.heading: Kinds of protection
sections.text:
• Copyright: protects creative works (books, music, films, software code). It exists as soon as the work is made.
• Patent: protects an invention, such as a new machine, for a number of years.
• Trademark: protects brand names and logos.
In Cameroon, copyright is protected by law; OAPI, based in Yaoundé, handles patents and trademarks for its member states.

sections.heading: Respecting IP
sections.text:
• Software piracy (using unlicensed copies) and selling copied films or music are illegal and harm creators.
• Plagiarism means presenting someone else's work as yours. Quote with quotation marks and give the source, or explain in your own words and cite where it came from.
• Use licensed or free open-source software, and ask permission before using others' photos or music.

worked_example.problem: Kum copies a paragraph from a website into his project without saying where it came from. What has he done, and what should he do?
steps: Using someone else's words as if they were his own is plagiarism.
He should put the words in quotation marks and give the source, or write the idea in his own words and cite the source.
worked_example.answer: Plagiarism; he should quote and cite the source
